tldr: DeepSeek shipped V4.1-Flash-1017 with MIT-licensed weights and unchanged API pricing; its own numbers show Terminal-Bench 4.0 rising from 31.2 to 42.3 as it targets one-prompt 'wish-style' coding.

Politico reports Anthropic privately pitched Congress a federal frontier-AI safety bill, with a $1B-damage or 50-casualty threshold for halting a model; separately, the FT reports Anthropic offered Blackstone a yield above 10% in a roughly $60B chip financing (secondhand, snippet-level).
Taiwan plans to criminalise smuggling restricted AI chips and servers to China, and Replit's CEO says it no longer works with Anthropic, a claim that is disputed.

items.title: DeepSeek ships V4.1-Flash-1017, an RL-tuned update aimed at one-prompt 'wish-style' coding; price unchanged, MIT weights
items.original_title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017新版本发布：许愿式编程一键成真
items.summary: DeepSeek upgraded V4.1 Flash to V4.1-Flash-1017 on Oct 17, switching its web app, mobile app and API (still model name deepseek-flash) to the new version with pricing unchanged. The company says self-feedback reinforcement learning improved from-scratch project building such as game development and 3D modelling, with demos including a Forbidden City 3D model, a browser racing game and a Godot-based Portal 2 remake. Official comparison figures reported by Chinese outlets: Terminal-Bench 4.0 31.2 to 42.3 and ProgramBench 20.3 to 29.1. Weights are posted on Hugging Face and ModelScope under MIT; the HF card and OpenRouter listing both hit Hacker News (531 and 511 points).
items.why_it_matters: A cheap open-weight model closing on frontier coding agents at an unchanged price keeps pressure on US coding-model pricing. It is also the first DeepSeek model refresh since the September V4.1 Flash launch and follows the week's outage.
key_numbers: MIT license, weights on HF and ModelScope

items.title: Anthropic privately pitches Congress a federal frontier AI safety bill, Politico reports
items.summary: Politico reported on Oct 16 that Anthropic circulated a confidential draft federal frontier-AI safety bill to members of Congress, and Bloomberg and Reuters followed. Per secondhand accounts, the government could seek to halt a model only for a foreseeable, imminent catastrophic threat (over $1B in damages or more than 50 people killed or seriously injured, tied to bioweapons, loss of control or cyberattacks), with judicial approval required and only Commerce able to seek the order. Independent evaluators would register with Commerce and emergent risks would be reported within 72 hours. Anthropic says it reflects its Advanced AI Framework.
items.why_it_matters: A leading lab drafting the federal rules for halting frontier models shapes the preemption debate before the midterms.
key_numbers: Commerce Dept sole authority to seek a halt order

items.title: Taiwan to make smuggling restricted AI servers and chips to China a crime, minister tells Bloomberg
items.summary: Taiwan's economy minister told Bloomberg that AI servers and advanced semiconductors will be added to a controlled-items list, after which shipping restricted AI hardware to China becomes a criminal offence under the Foreign Trade Act. Reports link the move to commitments in the 2026 US-Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade, say penalties and start date are undecided, and note a DPP lawmaker has drafted a mainland-China chip clause. Prosecutors have so far relied on forgery and breach-of-trust laws, including an August indictment of nine people over 74 Nvidia B300 servers.
items.why_it_matters: Closes a legal gap in a key chip-diversion route and aligns Taipei with US export controls.
key_numbers: 74 Nvidia B300 servers in August indictment

items.title: Anthropic offers Blackstone over 10% yield in roughly $60B Google TPU chip financing, FT reports
items.summary: The FT, relayed by Reuters on Oct 16, reports Anthropic is offering Blackstone a double-digit yield on its latest chip-financing deal, called Project North Star. Blackstone funds would take about $9B of an $18B junior tranche backed by Anthropic's five-year chip lease payments, with $42B of Broadcom-backed senior debt, funding roughly 1.5GW of Google TPUs. Similarly rated borrowers reportedly pay about 7% in public markets; the deal has not closed and Blackstone declined to comment.
items.why_it_matters: The price Anthropic pays for compute debt is a live signal on AI capex financing stress amid the semiconductor sell-off.

items.title: Anthropic's Jack Clark cites AI scenario of ~$44T US GDP by 2030 at IMF/World Bank meetings
items.summary: Speaking at the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Jack Clark said an Anthropic internal economic model shows AI could lift US output to about $44 trillion by 2030. Reports say that is the extreme case of three scenarios in Anthropic's Economic Scenario Explorer ($34.1T modest, $36.3T substantial, $44.4T extreme), not a point forecast. He also called for international cooperation on rules.
items.why_it_matters: Frontier-lab economic claims feed the investment narrative at a moment of AI-spending doubts.

English trade coverage cites 19.2% all-pass on Harvey LAB across 24 practice areas (12.5 points above its base model, scored by Vals) and parity with frontier closed models on LegalBench and PLawBench; one outlet lists 320B parameters. items.title: Nvidia says RTX 5090 is not discontinued but concedes supply is constrained
items.summary: Nvidia SVP Jeff Fisher told Taiwanese media at the RTX Spark launch in Taipei on Oct 16 that the RTX 5090 is still in production and will keep shipping, while admitting supply is tight.
